title: Missing Rebex license is silently ignored at startup; pooled SSH and terminals fail later with an opaque error
existing_state: Program.Main resolves the Rebex key from assembly metadata → rebex.key file → REBEX_LICENSE_KEY env var, and if all three are absent it simply skips setting Rebex.Licensing.Key and continues (Program.cs:17-40, the `if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(rebexKey))` at :37-40 has no else). Nothing in Services/ checks licensing either (only test-seam comments mention it). The user finds out only when they enable connection pooling or open an interactive terminal and Rebex throws its licensing exception mid-workflow — long after the cause (a build/environment issue) is visible.
recommendation: After the three-tier resolution in Program.cs, if rebexKey is empty, record a static flag (e.g. RebexLicenseState.Missing). In Form1, surface it once: a status-bar warning or a tooltip/disable on the pooling checkbox and Interactive Terminal menu item — 'Rebex license key not found (set REBEX_LICENSE_KEY or place rebex.key next to the exe); pooled sessions and terminals are unavailable.' Plain SSH.NET execution keeps working untouched.
user_benefit: Anyone building from source without the env var (a contributor, or the owner on a new machine) learns at launch why terminals/pooling will not work, instead of decoding a Rebex exception during a live session against production devices.

evidence.note: Three-tier key resolution with silent continue when no key is found
